'''Oded Regev''' ([[Hebrew language|Hebrew]]: עודד רגב; born 1978) is an Israeli-American [[theoretical computer scientist]] and mathematician. He is a professor of computer science at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences|Courant institute]] at [[New York University]].<ref>{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences |url=https://cs.nyu.edu/theory-group/faculty.html | title=Theoretical Computer Science Faculty listing |access-date=2024-01-16}}</ref> He is best known for his work in [[lattice-based cryptography]], and in particular for introducing the [[learning with errors]] problem.

== Biography ==

Oded Regev earned his B.Sc. in 1995, M.Sc. in 1997, and Ph.D. in 2001, all from [[Tel Aviv University]]. He completed his Ph.D. at the age of 21, advised by Yossi Azar, with a thesis titled "Scheduling and Load Balancing."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cs.tau.ac.il/thesis/ |title=School of Computer Science Thesis Repository |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=Tel Aviv University - Dept. of Computer Science |access-date=2024-01-16}}</ref><ref name="Oded Regev PhD thesis">{{cite web | title=Scheduling and Load Balancing | last=Regev | first=Oded | website=Tel Aviv University | url=https://primage.tau.ac.il/libraries/theses/exeng/free/1509397_abe.pdf | access-date=2024-01-16 | archive-date=2024-01-16 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240116205924/https://primage.tau.ac.il/libraries/theses/exeng/free/1509397_abe.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref> He held faculty positions at [[Tel Aviv University]] and the [[École Normale Supérieure]] before joining the Courant institute.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/people/oded-regev/|title=Oded Regev|author=<!--Not stated--> |date=October 5, 2014|website=Simons Foundation}}</ref>

== Work ==
Regev has done extensive work on [[Lattice (group)|lattices]]. He is best known for introducing the [[learning with errors]] problem (LWE).<ref name="Chita 2018 Gödel Prize">{{cite web | title=2018 Gödel Prize | website=European Association for Theoretical Computer Science (EATCS) | url=https://eatcs.org/index.php/component/content/article/1-news/2670-2018-godel-prize | access-date=2024-01-16}}</ref> As the citation reads:
<blockquote>
Regev’s work has ushered in a revolution in cryptography, in both theory and practice. On the theoretical side, LWE has served as a simple and yet amazingly versatile foundation for nearly every kind of cryptographic object imaginable—along with many that were unimaginable until recently, and which still have no known constructions without LWE. Toward the practical end, LWE and its direct descendants are at the heart of several efficient real-world cryptosystems.
</blockquote>
Regev's most influential other work on lattices includes [[cryptanalysis]] of the [[GGH signature scheme|GGH]] and [[NTRUSign|NTRU]] signature schemes in joint work with Phong Q. Nguyen, for which they won a best paper award at Eurocrypt 2006; introducing the [[Ring learning with errors|ring learning with errors problem]] in joint work with Chris Peikert and Vadim Lyubashevsky; and proving a converse to [[Minkowski's theorem]] and exploring its applications in joint works with his student Noah Stephens-Davidowitz and his former postdoc Daniel Dadush.
<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iacr.org/cryptodb/data/bestpapers.php|title=IACR Publication Awards|author=<!--Not stated--> |website=International Association for Cryptologic Research}}</ref>
<ref name="NguyenRegev2008">{{cite journal|last1=Nguyen|first1=Phong Q.|last2=Regev|first2=Oded|title=Learning a Parallelepiped: Cryptanalysis of GGH and NTRU Signatures|journal=Journal of Cryptology|volume=22|issue=2|year=2008|pages=139–160|issn=0933-2790|doi=10.1007/s00145-008-9031-0|s2cid=2164840|doi-access=free}}</ref>
<ref name="LyubashevskyPeikert2010">{{cite book|last1=Lyubashevsky|first1=Vadim|last2=Peikert|first2=Chris|last3=Regev|first3=Oded|title=Advances in Cryptology – EUROCRYPT 2010|chapter=On Ideal Lattices and Learning with Errors over Rings|series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science|volume=6110|year=2010|pages=1–23|issn=0302-9743|doi=10.1007/978-3-642-13190-5_1|isbn=978-3-642-13189-9}}</ref>
<ref>{{citation

<ref name="DadushRegev2016">{{cite book|last1=Dadush|first1=Daniel|last2=Regev|first2=Oded|title=2016 IEEE 57th Annual Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science (FOCS)|chapter=Towards Strong Reverse Minkowski-Type Inequalities for Lattices|year=2016|pages=447–456|doi=10.1109/FOCS.2016.55|arxiv=1606.06913|isbn=978-1-5090-3933-3|s2cid=16828584}}</ref>

In addition to his work on lattices, Regev has also done work in a large number of other areas in theoretical computer science and mathematics. These include [[quantum computing]], [[communication complexity]], [[hardness of approximation]], [[online algorithm]]s, [[combinatorics]], [[Probability theory|probability]], and [[dimension reduction]]. He has also recently become interested in topics in biology, and particularly [[RNA splicing]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cims.nyu.edu/~regev/.|title = Oded Regev|author=<!--Not stated--> |website=Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=3-gk0ioAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao|title=Oded Regev|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

Regev is an associate editor in chief of the journal ''[[Theory of Computing]],''<ref>{{cite web
 | url = https://theoryofcomputing.org/editors.html
 | title = Editors
 | website =Theory of Computing
 | access-date =2024-01-16
}}</ref> and is a co-founder and organizer of the TCS+ online seminar series.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/site/plustcs/|title=TCS+|website=sites.google.com}}</ref>

In August 2023 Regev published a preprint<ref>{{cite arXiv |last=Regev |first=Oded |date=2023 |title=An Efficient Quantum Factoring Algorithm |eprint=2308.06572|class=quant-ph}}</ref><ref>{{Cite report |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/surprising-and-supercool-quantum-algorithm-offers-faster-way-hack-internet-encryption |title='Surprising and super cool.' Quantum algorithm offers faster way to hack internet encryption |date=2023-09-19 |doi=10.1126/science.adk9418 |language=en|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Brubaker |first=Ben |date=2023-10-17 |title=Thirty Years Later, a Speed Boost for Quantum Factoring |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/thirty-years-later-a-speed-boost-for-quantum-factoring-20231017/ |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=Quanta Magazine |language=en}}</ref> describing an algorithm to factor integers with <math>\sim O(n^{3/2})</math> quantum gates which would be more efficient than [[Shor's algorithm]] which uses <math>\sim O(n^{2})</math>, but would require more qubits <math>\sim O(n^{3/2})</math> of quantum memory against Shor's <math>\sim O(n)\ </math>. A variant has been proposed<ref>{{Cite arXiv |last1=Ragavan |first1=Seyoon |last2=Vaikuntanathan |first2=Vinod |date=2023 |title=Optimizing Space in Regev's Factoring Algorithm |eprint=2310.00899|class=quant-ph}}</ref> that could reduce the space to around the same amount.

==Recognition==
Regev was a 2005 recipient of the Krill Prize.<ref name="Wolf Foundation 2005 Krill Prize"/> He won the 2018 [[Gödel Prize]] for his work on learning with errors.<ref name="Chita 2018 Gödel Prize"/> He was named as an [[ACM Fellow]], in the 2025 class of Fellows, "for contributions to computational complexity, lattice-based cryptography, and quantum computing".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.acm.org/media-center/2026/january/fellows-2025|title=Excellence and Impact Recognized by World's Preeminent Computing Society: Association for Computing Machinery Selects 71 Professionals for Outstanding Achievements|publisher=ACM|date=21 January 2026|access-date=2026-01-11}}</ref>
